header: THE SEARCH BAR AND THE PAX EDITOR (step 64a). When a sentence means "change the PAX directory" (intent.ts), the omnibar either
- opens the editor (a panel in the answer area) for the HOD of C&IT and for an executive he has authorised,
- or says plainly why not: nobody is logged in; the person has no authority; a delegate asked to authorise somebody (only the HOD does that).
The decision uses the LOGIN's ticket (the omnibar's userKey), never anything typed. I read the sentence first (pure); I ask the database only when it IS such a sentence.

members.name: nameOf
doc: I send the logged-in person's name with the answer (optional: without it the panel asks for the name itself).

behaviours: the HOD asking to add a pax number gets the editor (op add, role hod)
...with the number and the department already in the form
'delete pax 42046' opens the delete search on that number
the HOD asking to delegate gets the editor on the people tab (op delegate)
an authorised executive gets the editor, as a delegate
an authorised executive asking to authorise or revoke is told that only the HOD does that (no editor)
nobody logged in: asked to log in, no editor
logged in without authority: 'Not allowed', and it says who can
when the authority cannot be read, the editor is NEVER opened on doubt
the person is the login's ticket: the ticket is what is asked, whatever the sentence says ('add pax as 400001')
"${q}" is not a request to change the directory: null, and nobody is asked
...the database is never asked about a sentence that is not such a request
runOmnibar: the HOD's sentence returns the editor, tagged with the feedback source of the other PAX answers, attempt 1
...it never reached the PAX search, the hospital route, the model or the model's client; the ticket given is the login's
a QUESTION about the directory still goes to the PAX search (the editor route read it and let it pass)
a stranger's sentence returns the plain message, never the editor
a RETRY (a 'No' on an earlier answer) does not open the editor again
a failing editor route never breaks the omnibar: the other routes go on
an older caller without the dependency still works (optional, like the others)
omnibar.ts wires the editor route to the application's own connection (getDb) and to authorityForTicket
...never to the model's client (withClient, nlq_reader, NL2SQL_DATABASE_URL)
...and the editor route comes BEFORE the PAX search in runOmnibar
the modal draws the editor when the answer carries it, before the other cards
the request route takes the person from the login (sessionActor), checks the origin, and never reads a ticket from the body
...its code never touches the model's client either
the tables of the editor are not in the model's schema: no nlq view or prompt mentions them
the HOD's name is in the payload that opens the editor (so the header has it at once, with no request)
an authorised executive's own name is sent, trimmed
a blank name is left out of the payload (the panel will ask for it)
if the name cannot be read the editor STILL opens, without a name
without a name function (as before) the payload is what it always was
a person with no authority gets a plain sentence and his name is not sent anywhere
a question about the directory (not a change request) never reaches the name lookup
the authority and the name are asked TOGETHER (both start before either answers): the name adds no waiting
the search bar's wiring hands the editor the directory's name function (the one the session's actor already uses)
